name: Interferon alpha hair straightening

lead: Interferon alfa is a prescription drug used for hepatitis C and certain cancers. In a few case reports, patients with naturally curly hair experienced progressive straightening of the hair during treatment, which reversed after stopping. It is discussed online as a curiosity about how drugs can alter hair follicles.
It is not a cosmetic treatment: the drug has substantial systemic side effects, and the hair change in reports came alongside thinning and a rough texture.

paras: The documented cases occurred in patients receiving interferon alfa-2b with ribavirin under medical supervision for hepatitis C. The change developed over about three months and resolved over months after treatment ended.
Interferon alfa carries systemic side effects, and hair thinning and telogen effluvium were reported alongside the straightening. It is prescribed for medical conditions only.

angle.text: The straightening is a side effect of a prescription drug, reversing when treatment ends. It illustrates that hair shape can change with drugs, not a way to straighten hair.

lead: Interferon alpha hair straightening refers to the reported change of naturally curly hair into straight hair during treatment with interferon alfa, a drug used for chronic hepatitis C and some cancers [1].

A 2002 letter from Montpellier in the British Journal of Dermatology described two patients with naturally curly hair who developed acquired straightening on interferon alfa-2b plus ribavirin. The first, a 58-year-old man, noticed diffuse scalp thinning and complete straightening of scalp and body hair after about three months, with a rough, straw-like texture, more grey hair and longer eyebrows. The curls regrew after treatment ended and the changes recurred when pegylated interferon was started [1].
Because the effect arises as a drug side effect, it is reported in the medical literature and discussed in hair forums rather than used as a styling method.
infobox: Bessis et al., Br J Dermatol, 2002 [1]

paras: In the 2002 report, patient 1 began interferon alfa-2b 3 million units thrice weekly with ribavirin in January 1999. About three months later he had diffuse thinning and progressive complete straightening of scalp and body hair. Treatment stopped at 11 months for non-response, curly hair regrew over following months and normalized about two months later. When pegylated interferon with ribavirin began in October 2000, the same changes recurred after about three months [1].

Investigations showed telogen effluvium (40% telogen hairs, against a normal 10-20%), mild variation in hair shaft diameter on electron microscopy and a lymphocytic infiltrate around the hair bulb on scalp biopsy; ferritin, thyroid hormone, copper, zinc and selenium were normal [1].
No controlled studies found. The evidence is case reports, including the 2002 letter [1].

timeline.event: Bessis and colleagues report two cases of hair straightening on interferon alfa-2b and ribavirin [1].
